body.stem: You create a new security group with a Dynamic User membership type in Microsoft Entra ID. The group must include every member user in the tenant while excluding every guest user. The membership should update on its own whenever user accounts change. Which rule should you enter?

exhibit.text:
User properties supported in dynamic membership rules:
- user.objectId : GUID of the user object (null check selects all users)
- user.userType  : member | guest
- user.accountEnabled : true | false

Operators: -eq, -ne, -and, -or

options.text: user.objectId -ne null
(user.objectId -ne null) -and (user.userType -eq "Member")
user.accountEnabled -eq true
(user.objectId -ne null) -or (user.userType -eq "Member")

explanation.correct: Per the Microsoft Entra documentation on dynamic membership groups, to include every member user while excluding guest users, combine a non-null objectId check with a userType equality check joined with -and.

perChoice.a: user.objectId -ne null returns every user object in the directory regardless of userType, so guest users would still be included.
perChoice.c: user.accountEnabled -eq true returns every enabled user, which includes enabled guest accounts; it does not filter by user type.
perChoice.d: The -or operator makes either condition sufficient. Because user.objectId -ne null is true for every user, this rule includes both members and guests.

body.stem: You need to update the Usage location for 150 users in Microsoft Entra ID by using the Microsoft Entra admin center. You must complete the update using the minimum number of clicks. Which action should you take?

exhibit.text:
Tenant: Contoso Ltd.
Total user accounts: 250
User accounts needing update: 150
Property to update: Usage location
New value to apply: US

Current value (before update): various countries (US, IN, GB, etc.)

options.text: On the All Users page, select all 150 users at the same time and then use the Edit properties option to apply the new value in a single action
On the All Users page, select the users in groups of 60 or fewer, and run the Edit action for each group
On the All Users page, open each user profile individually and change the Usage location one at a time
Export the users to a CSV file, edit the Usage location in the file, and then use the Bulk create users option to import the changes

explanation.correct: The Microsoft Entra documentation states that on the All Users page you can select up to 60 users at a time and update their attributes at once. With 150 users to update, you batch them in groups of 60 (or fewer) and run the Edit action for each group.

perChoice.a: The bulk edit operation only supports up to 60 selected users at a time; selecting all 150 at once is not permitted by the interface.
perChoice.c: Editing each user profile individually works but is not the minimum-clicks approach the question requires.
perChoice.d: The Bulk create users option is for creating new user accounts, not updating the Usage location of existing accounts; this would not update the 150 existing users.

body.stem: You have a Security group and a Microsoft 365 group in Microsoft Entra ID (details in the exhibit). You need to add the Microsoft 365 group as a direct member of the Security group. Which outcome should you expect?

exhibit.text:
Group : Marketing Team
Type  : Security
Members: assigned

Group : Finance Comms
Type  : Microsoft 365
Members: assigned

options.text: The nesting succeeds, and every member of the Microsoft 365 child group inherits the access assigned to the Security parent group
The nesting isn't supported, so adding the Microsoft 365 group as a member of the Security group fails
The two groups merge into a single Security group whose membership combines the original members
The nesting succeeds for membership scopes only, but the Microsoft 365 group is excluded from any access assignments inherited from the parent

explanation.correct: Per the Microsoft Entra groups documentation, adding Microsoft 365 groups as members of security groups is one of the cross-type nesting scenarios that is not supported.

perChoice.a: The two group types cannot be nested in this direction; the operation is not allowed at all, so there is no inherited access scenario.
perChoice.c: There is no merge operation between an existing Security group and an existing Microsoft 365 group in the Entra admin center.
perChoice.d: Microsoft 365 groups cannot be nested into security groups at all; the entire addition fails rather than succeeding for a subset of scopes.

body.stem: The employee in the exhibit is known throughout the company by a shorter name than the one currently stored in the directory. Microsoft 365 apps build the name they display from either the first and last name held in Microsoft Entra ID or from the display name, and your organization requires that every app show the last name first and the name the employee wants to be seen as. Which set of name property values should you enter?

options.text: First name: Chris; Last name: Green; Display name: Green, Chris
First name: Chris; Last name: Green; Display name: Chris Green
First name: Christopher; Last name: Green; Display name: Green, Christopher
First name: Green; Last name: Chris; Display name: Green, Chris

explanation.correct: The name guidance says the first and last name fields should hold the name the user expects to see rather than the legal name on identification documents, and that the display name field is where the organization's preferred ordering is expressed. With a last-name-first convention and an employee who goes by Chris, the result is First name: Chris, Last name: Green, Display name: Green, Chris — the example given in the documentation. Apps that use the first and last name and apps that use the display name then render the same person consistently.

perChoice.b: The display name keeps the first name before the last name, so it ignores the organization-wide ordering and apps that render the display name disagree with apps that render the first and last name.
perChoice.c: The fields keep the legal name from the user's identity documents instead of the name the employee is known by, so apps that render the first and last name show a name the employee does not use.
perChoice.d: The ordering is applied to the first and last name fields themselves, which turns the family name into the given name; apps that render the first and last name then show "Green Chris", and the last name no longer matches the family name.

body.stem: Your marketing team wants a group that maintains itself from directory data, and the rule must pull in every account that has at least one secondary email address at contoso.com. The records in the show who should end up in the group once the rule is processed. Which expression should you use for the group's membership?

options.text: (user.otherMails -any (_ -endsWith "@contoso.com"))
(user.otherMails -contains "@contoso.com")
(user.otherMails -eq "@contoso.com")
(user.mail -endsWith "@contoso.com")

explanation.correct: otherMails is a multi-value string collection, and the documented way to test items inside such a collection is the underscore syntax combined with the -any or -all operator. Writing (user.otherMails -any (_ -endsWith "@contoso.com")) evaluates to true when at least one stored secondary address ends with @contoso.com, so it matches priya.shah@contoso.com (pshah@contoso.com) and dan.iversen@northwind.com (dan.iversen@contoso.com) and excludes the two accounts with no secondary address.

perChoice.b: -contains performs a partial string match, and the documentation explicitly notes that it does not perform matches for items in a collection, so it cannot be used to test the values held in otherMails.
perChoice.c: -eq compares the property against a single value, but otherMails is a collection of values. Comparing the whole collection to one address does not select users who hold that address as one of their secondary addresses.
perChoice.d: mail holds the user's primary SMTP address, not the secondary addresses in otherMails. In the exhibit, dan.iversen@northwind.com must be included but his mail value is @northwind.com, and priya.shah is matched only through otherMails.

body.stem: You need the members of a security group called Regional device policy - West to receive the same access as the members of one of the groups listed in the exhibit, and you plan to achieve that by adding the West group as a member of the group you choose. Which group in the exhibit should you choose?

columns: Microsoft Entra roles can be assigned to the group

options.text: The security group that was created in Microsoft Entra ID, isn't synchronized from on-premises Active Directory, and doesn't have the option for assigning Microsoft Entra roles enabled.
The Microsoft 365 group that was created in Microsoft Entra ID.
The security group that is synchronized from on-premises Active Directory.
The security group that has the option for assigning Microsoft Entra roles enabled.

explanation.correct: Nested groups are supported for the security group type, and the guidance's example adds one security group to another security group in Microsoft Entra ID. Of the four candidates, Device policy - All regions is a security group that lives in the cloud, is not synchronized from on-premises Active Directory, and was not created with the option to assign Microsoft Entra roles to its members, so the West group can be added to it and its members receive the parent's access.

perChoice.b: Adding a security group as a member of a Microsoft 365 group is one of the combinations that isn't supported; a group of this type can't be used as the container.
perChoice.c: Adding a group to a group that is synchronized with on-premises Active Directory isn't supported, so Legacy workstations can't act as the parent.
perChoice.d: A group that was created with the option for assigning Microsoft Entra roles to its members can't itself contain other groups, so Tenant administrators can't act as the parent.

body.stem: You are authoring a multi-expression membership rule for a dynamic membership group in Microsoft Entra ID. Operators are evaluated according to the precedence tiers documented for dynamic membership rules. Place each operator in the tier that reflects its position in the precedence order (highest to lowest).

explanation.correct: Per the precedence order documented for dynamic membership operators, -eq is grouped with the other comparison operators (-ne, -startsWith, -contains, -match, -in) on the highest tier; -not occupies the next tier; -and follows -not; -or follows -and; and -any/-all share the lowest tier because they iterate over collection items.

perChoice.eq: Tier 1 (evaluated first): -eq is a comparison operator that shares the highest precedence tier with -ne, -startsWith, -notStartsWith, -contains, -notContains, -match, -notMatch, -in, and -notIn.
perChoice.not: Tier 2: -not is the negation operator applied after the comparison operators.
perChoice.and: Tier 3: -and is the logical conjunction applied after -not.
perChoice.or: Tier 4: -or is the logical disjunction applied after -and and above the collection iterators.
perChoice.any: Tier 5 (evaluated last): -any iterates over a multi-value property to test per-item conditions, so it sits at the lowest precedence tier together with -all.

body.stem: You are writing expressions for a dynamic membership rule in Microsoft Entra ID. The data type of each user property determines which operators and value syntax you can use with it. Match each user property to the data type the documentation assigns to it.

explanation.correct: According to the property type table for dynamic membership rules, accountEnabled is documented as a Boolean property, employeeHireDate is documented under the Date/time property type (it accepts a DateTimeOffset value), department is a single-valued String property, and proxyAddresses is a String collection that requires the -any/-all collection iterators in expressions.

perChoice.acct: Boolean: the accountEnabled property only accepts the values true or false.
perChoice.hire: DateTimeOffset value: the employeeHireDate property accepts any DateTimeOffset value (or the keyword system.now) and enables the -le/-ge comparison operators.
perChoice.dept: Single string: the department property accepts one string value (or null), so it uses straightforward -eq/-startsWith comparisons.
perChoice.proxy: String collection: the proxyAddresses property is a multi-value list of SMTP addresses, which is why it must be evaluated with the -any collection iterator rather than scalar operators.

body.stem: You are granting an administrator the narrowest built-in Microsoft Entra directory role that still allows them to perform a maintenance task in a Microsoft Entra tenant. Match each task to the lowest-privilege built-in role that can perform it.

items.text: Bring external collaborators into the directory
Create a new account in the directory
Grant built-in Microsoft Entra directory permissions

explanation.correct: Per the role prerequisites documented for Microsoft Entra ID, inviting external people into the directory is restricted to the Guest Inviter role; creating a new account is the lowest-privilege task of the User Administrator role; granting Microsoft Entra directory permissions to users requires the Privileged Role Administrator; and managing tenant-wide user settings (such as LinkedIn account linking and the admin-portal restriction) requires the Global Administrator.

perChoice.invite: Guest Inviter: only this role (or higher) is documented for bringing external users into the directory as guests.
perChoice.create: User Administrator: this is the least-privileged role that the prerequisites table lists for creating a new account.
perChoice.roleassign: Privileged Role Administrator: the prerequisites explicitly call out this role for granting Microsoft Entra directory permissions to users.
perChoice.settings: Global Administrator: tenant-wide user settings in the User settings blade require this role rather than the more scoped User Administrator.

body.stem: You need to update several properties for a user in Microsoft Entra ID. Each property is grouped under one of the user profile categories shown on the user's properties page. Match each property to its category.

explanation.correct: Per the six profile categories documented for Microsoft Entra user profile editing, first name is an Identity attribute; department sits with Job information; mobile phone belongs to Contact info; age group is one of the Parental controls options; and usage location belongs to Settings (along with the sign-in toggle).

perChoice.first: Identity: first name is documented as one of the identity values alongside last name, display name, and user principal name.
perChoice.dept: Job information: department is grouped with job title, employee type, manager, and hire date under the Job information category.
perChoice.mobile: Contact info: mobile phone is grouped with the other phone numbers and the street/postal address under Contact info.
perChoice.age: Parental controls: the age-group dropdown (Minor, Not adult, Adult) lives in the Parental controls category and drives the consent/legal-age-group classification.
perChoice.usage: Settings: usage location (the user's global location for sign-in) is one of the Settings-category attributes, not Contact info.

body.stem: You are building a dynamic membership rule that targets specific devices joined to your Microsoft Entra tenant. Each device property captures a specific piece of information about a device object. Match each device property to the kind of information it stores.

slots.label: Mobile platform or operating system family

explanation.correct: According to the device attribute table for dynamic membership rules, deviceOSType identifies the platform family (for example iPad, Windows, AndroidEnterprise); deviceModel stores the hardware's product identifier (such as 'iPad Air'); deviceOSVersion stores the specific OS build string (such as one starting with '10.0.1' for Windows 10); and accountEnabled is the Boolean flag that decides whether the device can sign in.

perChoice.ostype: Mobile platform or operating system family: deviceOSType stores high-level platform identifiers like iPad, iPhone, Android, Windows, or AndroidEnterprise.
perChoice.model: Equipment's product identifier: deviceModel stores the hardware model name (such as 'iPad Air' or 'Surface Pro 9').
perChoice.osver: Specific operating system build string: deviceOSVersion stores the full operating system version rather than just the platform family.
perChoice.enabled: Sign-in eligibility flag: accountEnabled is a Boolean mirroring whether the device object is allowed to authenticate.

body.stem: You need to create four groups in Microsoft Entra ID, each for a different purpose. Match each requirement to the group type you should create.

slots.label: Membership includes machine objects as well as people
The group needs a group email address option offered at creation time
Membership follows attributes stored on the machines themselves
Membership follows attributes stored on the people themselves

explanation.correct: Each requirement points to a different group type. Only a security group can hold machines and people together, because a Microsoft 365 group accepts users alone and a single dynamic rule can never mix the two entity types. The group email address option appears only when you pick the Microsoft 365 group type. The remaining two requirements separate the two dynamic membership types: a device-based group evaluates attributes held on the machine objects themselves (and its rule has to be typed in the text box), while a user-based group evaluates attributes held on the people themselves, and those are the rules the portal's rule builder can compose.

perChoice.i1: Fits the requirement for a group email address option offered at creation time. Picking this group type is what turns on that option; it isn't offered for the other types.
perChoice.i2: Fits the requirement that mixes machines and people in one group. A security group may hold either devices or users, whereas a Microsoft 365 group may hold only users, so the security group is the only type that covers both kinds of member.
perChoice.i3: Fits the requirement about attributes held on the people themselves. A user-based dynamic group evaluates user attributes, and the portal's rule builder supports building these rules.
perChoice.i4: Fits the requirement about attributes held on the machines themselves. Device rules may reference only device attributes, and the rule builder doesn't cover device-based groups, so such a rule is typed in the text box.

body.stem: An existing cloud-only user has no profile image, and an administrator needs to apply a new picture file by using the Microsoft Entra admin center.
body.statement: To apply the new image, the administrator should {{action}}.

options.text: open Edit properties and attach the picture under the Identity category
select the camera icon in the lower-right corner of the user's thumbnail
open the tenant's User settings page and run Apply picture
select the Properties tab, then edit the Job information category

explanation.correct: The documentation states to select the camera icon in the lower-right corner of the user's thumbnail while on the user's overview page, which is the documented path for changing a user's profile picture.

perChoice.action:a: Edit properties is the full-pane editor for text-based profile values grouped by category; the Identity category lists display name and user principal name, with no picture file field to attach.
perChoice.action:c: User settings configures tenant-wide defaults such as self-service app registration and guest access; it does not accept an individual user's profile picture file.
perChoice.action:d: The Properties tab edits text properties by category; Job information holds the job title, department, and manager and does not expose a picture upload field.

body.stem: Administrator needs to update the Title for one of the users shown in the exhibit. The change must not be overwritten when the next directory synchronization cycle runs.

exhibit.text:
Property         | Value
Identity source   | Windows Server Active Directory
Display name      | Jane Doe
Title             | Senior Engineer
Usage location    | US

body.statement: The administrator updates the Title using {{location}}.

options.text: the Identity category of the user's properties in the Microsoft Entra admin center
the Job information category of the user's properties in the Microsoft Entra admin center
the on-premises management console
the Settings category of the user's properties in the Microsoft Entra admin center

explanation.correct: The documentation states that for users whose source of authority is on-premises AD, identity, contact info, and job info must be updated on-premises; otherwise the next synchronization cycle overwrites the change.

perChoice.location:a: Identity is one of the categories the docs say must be updated on-premises for synced users; editing it in the cloud will be overwritten by the next sync.
perChoice.location:b: Job information is one of the categories the docs say must be updated on-premises for synced users, even though it is the right place logically; editing here is overwritten by the next sync.
perChoice.location:d: Settings holds sign-in state and usage location, not the Title; even if it did, updating in the cloud for a synced user would still be overwritten by sync.

body.stem: You need to create a dynamic membership group whose membership must always match the people whose Manager property is set to a specific employee in Microsoft Entra ID. As directory data changes, new people must be added automatically.

exhibit.text:
Field                | Value
Manager objectId     | aaaaaaaa-0000-1111-2222-bbbbbbbbbbbb
Subordinates         | 7

body.statement: The administrator enters {{rule}} in the text box.

options.text: user.manager.objectId -eq "objectId"
(user.objectId -ne null) -and (user.userType -eq "Member")
Direct Reports for "objectId"
(user.department -eq "Sales") -or (user.department -eq "Marketing")

explanation.correct: The documentation shows that the only supported syntax for a direct reports rule is `Direct Reports for "{objectID_of_manager}"`, which must be entered in the rule text box.

perChoice.rule:a: The Manager property is set on each user to identify their manager, but it is not a valid property name for a dynamic membership rule expression; the documented direct reports syntax uses the special `Direct Reports for` form.
perChoice.rule:b: This is the documented rule that adds every member user in the tenant; it does not scope to the direct reports of a single manager.
perChoice.rule:d: This rule filters by department and would include people from Sales or Marketing regardless of manager assignment; it does not match a specific manager's direct reports.

body.stem: You need a dynamic membership group whose rule uses -contains against a multi-value user attribute to identify members correctly. You must build the rule in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
body.statement: The administrator constructs the rule using {{tool}}.

options.text: the rule builder, which supports up to five expressions and exposes the -contains check
the text box, since -contains is one of the operators the rule builder does not expose
the Microsoft Graph SDK with PowerShell
the quick rule preset menu, which can auto-generate -contains expressions

explanation.correct: The documentation lists 'Rule with a -contains or -notContains operator' among the examples of advanced syntax that require the text box; the rule builder supports up to five simple expressions but does not expose -contains.

perChoice.tool:a: The rule builder supports up to five simple expressions but does not include -contains or -notContains; rules using these must use the text box.
perChoice.tool:c: Using the Graph SDK with PowerShell is a programming path outside the admin center UI; the question is about which entry surface inside the admin center supports the rule.
perChoice.tool:d: No preset menu exists in the admin center that auto-generates -contains expressions; rules with -contains must be entered manually in the text box.

body.stem: You administer Microsoft Entra groups in your tenant. Users are receiving welcome notifications by email whenever they are added to a new Microsoft 365 group. You want to stop this notification behavior for every group in the tenant, regardless of the membership type that each group uses.
body.statement: Because this behavior can be turned off only by running a command in {{tool}}, you should connect and disable it there.

options.text: Exchange PowerShell
Microsoft Graph PowerShell
Microsoft Entra admin center
Microsoft 365 admin center

explanation.correct: The documentation states that the welcome notification for Microsoft 365 groups can be turned off only in Exchange PowerShell, regardless of the membership type.

perChoice.tool:b: Graph PowerShell isn't documented for this setting.
perChoice.tool:c: That UI does not expose the welcome toggle.
perChoice.tool:d: That UI does not host the welcome toggle.

body.stem: You administer the Microsoft Entra directory for a K-12 school district. An import tool created the accounts listed below but left the parental controls section of every profile empty, so no age band has been recorded for any of them. You need to fill in the correct value for each account. Which set of values should you enter?

options.text: a.rios@contoso.edu = Minors; j.martin@contoso.edu = Not adult; t.nguyen@contoso.edu = Adults
a.rios@contoso.edu = Not adult; j.martin@contoso.edu = Minors; t.nguyen@contoso.edu = Adults
a.rios@contoso.edu = Minors; j.martin@contoso.edu = Adults; t.nguyen@contoso.edu = Not adult
a.rios@contoso.edu = Adults; j.martin@contoso.edu = Not adult; t.nguyen@contoso.edu = Minors

explanation.correct: The Parental controls category of a user profile records the age group, and the documented bands are: 12 and under is Minors, 13 to 18 years old is Not adult, and 18 and over is Adults. Applying that to the exhibit, the 12-year-old (a.rios) is Minors, the 16-year-old (j.martin) is Not adult, and the 19-year-old (t.nguyen) is Adults. The recorded age group together with the consent provided by parent options is what produces the legal age group classification, which can limit the user's access and authority, so getting the band right for each account matters.

perChoice.b: This reverses the two student accounts: a 12-year-old sits below the 13-year threshold and therefore belongs in the Minors band, while a 16-year-old falls in the 13-to-18 band and is not a minor. The 19-year-old value is correct here, but the other two are swapped.
perChoice.c: The 12-year-old and the 19-year-old are placed correctly, but a 16-year-old is not 18 or older, so it cannot take the Adults value; it belongs to the 13-to-18 band.
perChoice.d: This inverts the ranges: it treats the youngest account as the oldest band and the oldest account as the youngest band, which contradicts the documented boundaries of 12 and under, 13 to 18, and 18 and over.

body.stem: You are a User Administrator onboarding 12 new contractors. On the All users page of the Microsoft Entra admin center you select all 12 accounts and run the bulk update. The exhibit lists the changes the onboarding team requires, and you want to complete the work in as few separate operations as possible. Which statement is accurate?

columns: Change requested by the onboarding team
rows: Job title: Contractor to Senior contractor

options.text: City, Job title, Office location can be applied from this screen; Manager must be applied from each user profile
City, Job title, Office location, Manager can all be applied from this screen
Manager can be applied from this screen; City, Job title, Office location must each be applied from a user profile
Only City can be applied from this screen; Job title, Office location, Manager must each be applied from a user profile

explanation.correct: The Edit properties action offered when you select multiple users exposes only a fixed set of attributes: City, Company name, Country or region, Department, Employee hire date, Employee type, Job title, Office location, State or province, Street address, Usage location, and Zip or postal code. Three of the four requested changes (City, Job title, Office location) fall inside that list, so all 12 accounts can be updated in one bulk operation since 12 is well within the 60-account limit per edit. Manager is not part of the bulk list, and any other property must be changed by visiting the specific user profile, so the Manager value needs one profile visit per contractor.

perChoice.b: Not correct, because Manager is not one of the attributes that the Edit properties action exposes for a multi-user selection, so it cannot be applied from this screen no matter how the other fields are handled.
perChoice.c: This reverses the two groups. City, Job title and Office location are all on the list of properties offered by the bulk Edit properties action, while Manager is the requested change that is missing from it.
perChoice.d: Not correct, because Job title and Office location are both offered by the bulk Edit properties action, just like City. Of the four requested changes, Manager is the only one that needs a per-profile edit.

body.stem: You have a user whose identity is mastered in Windows Server Active Directory and synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID. You need to update a single attribute for the user right away, without modifying the on-premises directory and without waiting for the next synchronization cycle. Which attribute should you update directly in the Microsoft Entra admin center?
body.statement: The attribute that the Microsoft Entra documentation explicitly identifies as one you can change directly in the Microsoft Entra admin center for a user synchronized from Windows Server Active Directory is {{slot1}}.

options.text: Usage location
User principal name
Display name
Job title

explanation.correct: The documentation states that for users synced from Windows Server Active Directory, the identity, contact, and job information must be updated in the on-premises directory. However, you can update Microsoft Entra ID attributes directly in the Microsoft Entra admin center, and Usage Location is given as the explicit example of such an attribute.

perChoice.slot1:b: User principal name is listed by the documentation as one of the attributes synchronized from on-premises. The docs note that it can technically be updated in the cloud for users managed from on-premises, but doing so is not recommended except for emergency purposes.
perChoice.slot1:c: Display name is part of the user's identity information and is sourced from the on-premises directory, so for a synced user it must be edited in Windows Server Active Directory.
perChoice.slot1:d: Job title is part of the job information category, which the documentation says must be updated in Windows Server Active Directory for synced users.
